trap_name: Typical confusion trap: misapplying the exclusion period of a formative right as the 3-year ordinary limitation period
misconception: This is the pitfall most often hit by 64% of students across the university! General-purpose AI answering frequently applies the 3-year limitation period of Article 188 of the Civil Code to the right of revocation as well. The limitation of action governs claims, whereas the right of revocation is a formative right and must follow the strict statutory exclusion period!

trap_name: Norm-mismatch trap: conflating the statutory start points for fraud and for duress
misconception: The Civil Code strictly distinguishes fraud from duress: duress runs from the day the coercive act ends, whereas fraud runs from the day the party knew or ought to have known of the ground for revocation!

trap_name: Memorising obsolete provisions: conflating the old Contract Law with the current Civil Code
misconception: Uses a repealed provision of the old Contract Law. The current Civil Code uniformly sets the start point for fraud at 1 year, with a maximum protection period of 5 years (not 2 years).

trap_name: Memorising repealed law: equating a defect in the power of disposal with absolute invalidity of the sales contract
misconception: This is the traditional disaster zone that 58% of students easily fall into in law exams and postgraduate entrance exams! The Civil Code clearly distinguishes obligation acts (creditor contracts) from disposal acts (property-right changes). A sales contract is valid even without the power of disposal; failure to perform gives rise to breach liability, and a bona fide transferee is directly protected by bona fide acquisition!

trap_name: Rule-confusion trap: applying the redemption rule for lost property to a voluntarily entrusted item
misconception: Article 312 of the Civil Code provides a 2-year window to pay the price and demand return only for lost property and similar items that left the true owner possession against their will. In this case A voluntarily lent the item to B (a possessory entrustment), so the original owner must bear the trust risk; a right of redemption for consideration simply does not exist!

trap_name: Blind spot in the scope of the doctrine: bona fide acquisition spans both movable and immovable property
misconception: General-purpose AI often mixes up the delivery requirement for movables with the registration requirement for immovables. Bona fide acquisition is precisely a statutory original-acquisition regime resting on the twin pillars of the public credibility of possession for movables and of registration for immovables!

trap_name: Mechanical no-authority-negation trap: ignoring the commercial-appearance doctrine's tilt toward protecting bona fide third parties
misconception: Many beginners read only the half-sentence 'Zhang had resigned and had no authority' and mechanically hold the contract invalid. The very purpose of the apparent-authority doctrine is to force the principal to bear the legal consequences, when it created an appearance of authority, despite a substantive lack of authority!

trap_name: Reversed-procedural-ranking trap: downgrading apparent authority to the pending-effect status of narrow unauthorised agency
misconception: Once apparent authority is established, the counterparty has a choice: it may assert that the apparent-agency contract is valid and require the company to perform, or it may revoke on its own initiative. But the principal (the tech company) has no right at all to unilaterally void the contract by refusing ratification!

trap_name: Over-strict attribution-element trap: conflating attributability of the appearance of authority with tortious intent
misconception: Establishing apparent authority does not require the principal to have subjective fraudulent intent at all! Objective negligence such as poor control of the official seal or failure to recover a letter of authorisation suffices to create the appearance of authority and thus to establish the principal's attributability!

trap_name: Rote-learning trap on advanced concepts: a five-stage in-order pipeline cannot possibly exhibit WAR/WAW anti-dependencies!
misconception: This is a knowledge hallucination that general large models are very prone to produce! WAR hazards can occur only in superscalar processors that support out-of-order execution (such as the Tomasulo architecture). In a classic five-stage in-order pipeline instructions flow in order, and an earlier instruction can never read a register after a later instruction!

trap_name: Classification-confusion trap: mistaking register data transfer for a hardware structural resource conflict
misconception: A structural hazard means several instructions contending for the same physical unit in the same clock cycle (for example, a single-port memory being read for both an instruction and data). The stem is clearly about a value dependency between registers; that is a pure data hazard!

trap_name: Over-generalisation guessing trap: arithmetic instructions have no conditional branch
misconception: Control hazards are caused only by conditional branches (beq, bne) or unconditional jumps (jmp) modifying the PC; ordinary arithmetic instructions have no branch-prediction need whatsoever!

trap_name: Double trap of set-count calculation and replacement policy: conflating total cache blocks with sets
misconception: Many students directly treat 512 blocks as 512 sets and compute a 9-bit or 8-bit Index. More seriously, LRU based on temporal locality is the theoretical and engineering best baseline; FIFO not only has a higher miss rate but also triggers the famous Belady anomaly!

trap_name: Blind block-size increase trap: oversized blocks compress the number of sets and aggravate conflict misses
misconception: With total cache capacity fixed, blindly increasing block size halves the total number of sets, which makes conflict misses on strided accesses even worse and significantly raises the main-memory miss penalty!

trap_name: Component-responsibility mismatch trap: conflating instruction prefetching with data memory access
misconception: The instruction prefetch buffer targets adaptive fetch of sequential instruction streams and cannot reduce conflict misses for data-intensive array reads and writes that jump randomly with large strides!

trap_name: Classic high-risk confusion trap: mistaking a TLB miss for a page fault
misconception: This is the core pitfall where large models all over the web answer wrongly and 71% of students fail the final exam! A TLB miss merely means the page-table entry is not cached in the fast table; the physical page may well be sitting in physical memory. A genuine page fault is triggered only when the page-table lookup finds Valid=0 (the page has not been loaded into memory)!

trap_name: Exception-return semantics trap: applying the interrupt PC+4 return to a fault that re-executes the instruction
misconception: An interrupt is asynchronous and usually returns to the next instruction; a page fault is a fault, and the memory instruction has not successfully read its data, so jumping directly to the next instruction would load garbage into the registers and collapse the program logic!

trap_name: Flag-logic total inversion trap: Valid=1 means the page is in physical memory
misconception: A Valid/Present bit of 1 means the page is in a main-memory physical frame; only 0 means the page is unallocated or has been swapped out to the disk swap area!

trap_name: Confusing the boundary between unbiasedness and efficiency: equating insufficient estimation precision with a biased estimator
misconception: Many students, and general large models not constrained by graph facts, blurt out that the estimator is biased! Bias occurs only when key variables are omitted or endogeneity is present. Correlation among regressors never destroys unbiasedness!

trap_name: Theorem-condition comprehension trap: wrongly declaring the BLUE property invalid
misconception: Among all linear unbiased estimators, OLS is still the one with the smallest variance (BLUE); it is merely that this minimum variance has itself been pushed up by the sample data.

trap_name: Classic counter-intuitive surface trap: R-squared and F are often inflated under collinearity!
misconception: The most classic textbook symptom of multicollinearity is: the F test is extremely significant and R-squared is very high (e.g. 0.85), yet the t test for every regressor fails to reject the null hypothesis!

trap_name: Fatal blind spot on weak instruments: a large sample does not automatically rescue the severe bias of a weak instrument
misconception: This is the top empirical-econometrics disaster scene! When first-stage relevance is weak (F < 10), the asymptotic bias of 2SLS shifts toward OLS, the sampling distribution becomes extremely fat-tailed and distorted, conventional standard errors fail completely, and even devastating spurious causality can be produced!

trap_name: Mathematical blind spot on degrees of freedom and identification: exact identification makes a statistical exogeneity test impossible
misconception: Over-identification tests (such as the Sargan test / Hansen J statistic) require the number of instruments m to be strictly greater than the number of endogenous variables k (m > k). Under exact identification residuals are exactly orthogonal to fitted values, the residual-sum-of-squares degrees of freedom are 0, and no test can be performed at all!

trap_name: Exclusion restriction completely inverted: a valid instrument must never affect the dependent variable directly!
misconception: The strict definition of the exclusion restriction is: the instrument Z may affect wages only indirectly, through the single channel of the endogenous variable Educ. If Z itself directly determines wages, the variable enters the disturbance term of the original equation and exogeneity is gone!

trap_name: High-frequency property-confusion trap: misjudging impaired efficiency as the estimator losing unbiasedness
misconception: 60% of the class will blurt out that the OLS estimator is biased! The only precondition for unbiasedness is exogeneity E(u|X)=0. Whether residual variance grows or shrinks only enlarges or reduces the sampling fluctuation of the estimator; it never shifts the population average of the estimates systematically!

trap_name: Statistical-test mechanism confusion: equating the White test with a test that depends on a specific functional form
misconception: The White test's greatest breakthrough is precisely that it regresses squared residuals on the first-order, squared and interaction terms of all regressors, so the researcher need not guess which specific function the heteroskedasticity takes!

trap_name: WLS blind-faith anti-pattern: WLS with wrong weights is even worse than OLS
misconception: Feasible generalised least squares (FGLS/WLS) is asymptotically efficient only when the researcher guesses the heteroskedasticity function structure correctly. With a wrong weight matrix the WLS estimator actually loses consistency, which is why modern top empirical papers almost universally use OLS + robust standard errors!

trap_name: Traditional dogmatic waterfall trap: forcibly freezing requirements in volatile business domains
misconception: Many students new to software engineering blindly worship the rigour of the waterfall model and ignore that when external business or policy changes monthly, the strong dependencies between its phases plunge the whole team into endless requirement-change submission processes and wholesale code rewrites!

trap_name: Dogmatic misreading of the Agile Manifesto: equating embracing change with needing no documentation or architecture
misconception: The Agile Manifesto says working software over comprehensive documentation; it absolutely does not say no documentation! In safety-critical systems such as healthcare, finance and aerospace, requirement traceability matrices (RTMs) and interface contract documents are statutory one-vote-veto items!

trap_name: Anti-engineering development-pattern trap: the big-bang model is synonymous with chaotic engineering
misconception: The big-bang model, with no plan, no phase review and no test gate, violates every basic principle of software engineering and is the number-one anti-pattern that ruins the vast majority of software projects!

trap_name: Branch-proliferation code-smell trap: a serious violation of the Open-Closed Principle (OCP)
misconception: Extending the underlying implementation with masses of conditional branches (if-else) is the engineering smell beginners commit most often! Every new database requires modifying high-level business code and recompiling and retesting, easily causing regression bugs!

trap_name: Inheritance-abuse pitfall: a serious violation of the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
misconception: Graph databases and relational databases have no is-a substitutability relation at all in data model, transaction semantics or query contract! Forcing inheritance arbitrarily violates the base-class contract, and the subclass cannot safely substitute for the parent!

trap_name: God-class tight-coupling trap: creating a single point of failure and killing unit testing
misconception: Introducing a global all-purpose God Class is a typical anti-pattern: cohesion becomes extremely low and coupling extremely high, global state is chaotic, and unit tests can no longer mock dependencies at all!

trap_name: False-coverage-security trap: high line coverage is not high fault-detection power
misconception: This is the most dangerous blind spot in software-engineering quality gates! Test code executing every line does not mean it asserts the logical correctness of every line! If the test cases contain no assert at all, coverage can still show 100%, while the mutation kill rate drops straight to 0!

trap_name: Missing negative-testing trap: skipping out-of-boundary interception tests leads directly to production crashes
misconception: Testing only valid data (positive testing) is a typical symptom of fragile software. Robustness testing must cover the invalid equivalence classes immediately outside the boundary, ensuring exceptions are safely caught and controlled errors raised, rather than throwing uncaught exceptions that crash the system!

trap_name: Test-type conceptual mismatch trap: misjudging mutation testing as performance stress testing
misconception: Mutation testing is the famous advanced meta-testing technique of testing the tests, belonging to fault injection and test-suite capability evaluation, and has nothing to do with performance stress testing!
